scenes.text: Usually, I stand in one room and mistake its furniture for the whole building.
scenes.query: a person studying one furnished room while transparent floors and hidden rooms surround it

scenes.text: Attention widens, narrows, turns inward, and quietly changes what feels real.
scenes.query: an antique camera aperture opening and closing over a busy street and an inward-facing mirror

scenes.text: I can vanish into a book while my body waits in a chair, loyal as a coat.
scenes.query: an open book projecting a vast landscape above an occupied reading chair beside a hanging coat

scenes.text: When I return, the room remains. My spotlight simply stopped feeding it light.
scenes.query: a theater spotlight sweeping back onto a familiar living room after illuminating a distant stage

scenes.text: Different states of consciousness are different rooms receiving electricity.
scenes.query: a floor plan with separate rooms lighting one by one as power moves through copper lines

scenes.text: Joy can repaint a street. Grief can lower winter over a kitchen in July.
scenes.query: one city street split between radiant color and a summer kitchen covered by gentle indoor snow

scenes.text: The world did not swear allegiance to my mood. Mood became the glass through which it arrived.
scenes.query: colored glass panes rotating before the same landscape and changing its emotional atmosphere

scenes.text: A symbol is that glass made portable. It carries more than physical weight.
scenes.query: a small pane of stained glass carried in two hands, projecting an enormous scene onto a wall

scenes.text: A key is metal, permission, escape, or return, depending on which part of me holds it.
scenes.query: one antique key casting four shadows shaped like a gate, open road, locked room, and childhood home

scenes.text: The object stays still. Meaning circles it like weather around a mountain.
scenes.query: a motionless mountain-shaped stone surrounded by changing clouds, rain, sunlight, and snow

scenes.text: My private alphabet is built from childhood rooms, songs, smells, scars, and slamming doors.
scenes.query: a wooden type case filled with a toy, record, perfume bottle, bandage, and miniature door

scenes.text: Someone sees an old coat. I feel a hand from a winter that no longer exists.
scenes.query: an old coat in an empty hallway touched by a warm hand-shaped patch of winter sunlight

scenes.text: Symbols cannot be translated like receipts. The same image spends differently in every life.
scenes.query: a shop counter where the same brass token becomes different treasured objects for different customers

scenes.text: In dreams, one doorway can be birth, funeral, warning, and forgiveness at once.
scenes.query: a single doorway opening simultaneously into a nursery, candlelit memorial, storm path, and sunrise garden

scenes.text: The more exact a symbol becomes, the less sky it carries. Precision can trim off stars.
scenes.query: a craftsman fitting a tiny precise frame around a night sky while stars remain beyond its edges

scenes.text: Even blankness may work. A pause can be language backstage, changing costumes.
scenes.query: an empty theater stage while letters change costumes behind a half-open curtain

scenes.text: Nothing may be the workshop where tomorrow's image receives a handle.
scenes.query: a quiet workshop where an undefined glowing shape receives a carefully carved wooden handle

scenes.text: Multiple focus means I may exceed the room my waking mind rents.
scenes.query: a small rented room suspended inside a much larger transparent mansion filled with moving lights

scenes.text: Body, dream, art, and ritual may be alphabets writing one living sentence.
scenes.query: an open hand, sleeping face, painted canvas, and candle circle arranged as lines in one luminous manuscript

scenes.text: Now I look at one ordinary object and ask what invisible story it carries for me.
scenes.query: one familiar personal object resting on a wooden bedside table as dawn slowly fills the room
